title: Word: Copilot edits your document directly by default in chat
summary: Hold: the licensing discussion leaves editing entitlement unresolved even though Microsoft's service description identifies Edit with Copilot as a Premium feature requiring a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. The general statement about users without the add-on also omits the distinction between Basic app access and standalone Copilot Chat. The roadmap facts and both licence-assignment controls are supported.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center licence-assignment path is Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense with UserId, AddLicenses containing SkuId and empty RemoveLicenses assigns a user licence rather than configuring the editing default.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.quote: As an administrator, you can manage many Microsoft Copilot settings from Copilot > Settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.quote: This API is currently in preview. Supported settings: microsoft.copilot.copilotchatpinning; microsoft.copilot.blockaccesstoopenfiles; microsoft.copilot.imagegeneration; microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch; microsoft.copilot.allowinadmincenters.
claims.fix: Change 'its Microsoft Graph copilotPolicySetting page lists five supported settings' to 'its preview Microsoft Graph copilotPolicySetting page lists five supported settings'.
